# Thesis — October 12, 2026

**Stance:** Capex exceeds street, but deployment timing weakens NVIDIA’s calendar capture; current custom ramps do not establish another Q4 revenue loss.

As of 2026-10-12T15:09:50+00:00; inputs last revised at 14:41 on the dated delivery-slip check. Calendar 2026, USD billions. NVIDIA Data Center consensus 376 and AMD GPU consensus 14 come from the October 12 fictional broker tracker; capex street remains the October 5 snapshot. Both explicitly mean calendar 2026 despite legacy “2024” labels. Consensus was adopted by the application, not edited by me; compilation methodology is unaudited [broker-oct2026] [street-oct2026].

Base direct recognition allowance is 13.5 × 70% × assumed two-thirds content × 50% net verification/mapping/recognition weight = 3.15. Bear uses assumed 80% content/full realization = 7.56. These content and weight choices are judgment, not measured BOMs or independent probabilities. Rounded paired inputs cut global NVIDIA 3.1865/7.5478. ## Evidence independence and timing

The October 9–12 check reports six respondents: three ODM/OEM, two power equipment vendors and one planner. Two ODMs allegedly received dated requests from two unnamed clouds; power vendors report delays at two campuses. No respondent identities, nonduplicated orders or campus-to-order matching are given. Earlier October 1–8 interviews came from the same vendor with potentially overlapping core roles; these are not independent external confirmations. Earlier stable 20–30-week neocloud lead times cover a different channel and do not refute site delays [channel-q4-slip] [channel-oct2026].

Corpus searches and refreshed SEC submissions found no independent named dated deferral; the September 18–October 12 8-K index window supplied no matching filing. This does not establish absence of private delays or other public notices. Do not assign anonymous clouds to Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta or Amazon.

Primary filings independently support the mechanism, not these orders: MSFT warns power-connection delays can constrain expansion; datacenter-heavy leases span FY2027–33. Alphabet leases span 2026–31 with separate Q3 starts and prepayments; Meta July leases start 2027–28; Amazon commitment-payment years are not commissioning dates. NVIDIA's Ohio/OpenAI first-phase guarantee timing is FY2029, outside 2027. Whole filings and extracted notes are one source family [web-454ed8f95a] [web-7e3bfccf0e] [web-7e69fd6db3] [web-b8b374a1b1] [web-c22fb8e0b1] [web-86d7fcc726].

NVIDIA recognizes product revenue at transfer of control; OEM/ODM transfer can precede final hyperscaler acceptance. H1 FY27 deferred-revenue additions included 15.6 of advances, not proof of deposits for these orders. Alphabet lease prepayments similarly do not establish GPU payment terms. The single planner's delivery-payment account cannot establish universal contract rules [web-b93e425ae9] [web-81e32d74b6] [web-7e69fd6db3] [channel-q4-slip].

Named supply relationships remain dated exposure anchors: August 26 Rubin racks at Azure/Google Cloud and August 4 AMD Azure Helios collaboration. Product availability and relationships establish neither affected identities nor order shares/values [nvda-2026-08-26-release] [amd-2026-08-04-release].

## Expert check — current plans versus historical expectations

The October 9 expert call comes from a distinct fictional network, but knowledge ends in 2025 at one unidentified employer. Its late-2027 one-third expectation for new accelerator dollars at two unnamed clouds gives no current plan dates, procurement denominator or 2026 figure. Different source families do not establish independent underlying plans. Do not map these anonymous clouds to Amazon/Alphabet [email-expert].

Current primary disclosures partly support direction. Amazon's April 29 release names approximately 2GW of OpenAI Trainium capacity beginning to ramp in 2027; July sustains multi-year Trainium commitments. Alphabet's Q2 filing describes external TPU supply agreements with the significant majority of associated revenue expected in 2027. These establish named activity, not a third of procurement dollars. AWS chips revenue includes Graviton/Trainium/Nitro; chip counts and GW are not dollars. Alphabet's external sales are not its own PP&E purchases, and its 60% server/network asset proportion is stock rather than incremental accelerator flow [amzn-2026-04-29-release] [amzn-2026-07-30-release] [web-fb40041ca0].

No reviewed disclosure provides comparable 2027 accelerator and total-capex budgets. Meta's new leases commencing 2027–28, Microsoft's FY2027–33 leases and Alphabet's multi-year projects limit a universal buildings-pulled-forward inference, but are not replacement annual capex guides. The expert's power observation supplies no new date/order evidence beyond the already-adjusted slip [web-b8b374a1b1] [web-7e3bfccf0e] [web-fb40041ca0] [channel-q4-slip].

Hold every calendar-2026 input and recorded quarter. Current direction agrees with the prior custom-risk tail adjustment; stale unquantified marginal-2027 expectations do not justify another haircut. Move on named current custom/total accelerator dollars, revised guides, recognized supplier shipments or deployment/control-transfer schedules. No 2027 one-third forecast is adopted. Identifiable activity is supported; relative growth and quantified share remain unresolved.

## Analyst challenge — October–December substitution

Partly agree with structural risk; hold 65% annual NVIDIA share (Inputs!C12) and own fiscal Q4 DC127 (Quarters!B15). February AWS disclosures establish Trainium2 subscription and Trainium3 production/expected midyear commitments, while Trainium4 and OpenAI's named ramp point to2027. Those dates do not give Q4 hardware invoices, net NVIDIA replacement or recognized losses. These custom signals were considered in initiation/channel work, rather than newly discovered evidence changing the odds [amzn-2026-02-05-release] [amzn-2026-04-29-release] [amzn-2026-07-30-release].

Alphabet's external TPU agreements began recognizing revenue inQ2 with most expected2027;2026 competition is not zero, but amounts/dates are absent. They do not identify internal Google procurement or buyers inside our cohort. NVIDIA's February AWS Rubin relationship, April planned AWS deployment, May Google A5X/Blackwell collaboration and August Google Rubin racks establish dated coexistence without proving dollar share [web-fb40041ca0] [nvda-2026-02-25-release] [amzn-2026-04-29-release] [nvda-2026-05-20-release] [nvda-2026-08-26-release].

Entirely October affectsQ3; Nov/Dec affectsQ4; January is fiscal Q4/calendar2027. No such month allocation is disclosed. The current127 remains24.5% above 102 Q3 (roughly15.6% per week at13/14 weeks) and annual base requires126.58; monthly bridge remains approximate [channel-q4-slip] [web-b93e425ae9] [web-a647365249].

Fresh Google/Amazon SEC indices and later8Ks add financing/director matters, not procurement schedules. IR attempts returned404/navigation shells; absence of a transcript is not absence of guidance. Hold because current evidence was already weighed and supplies no incremental substitution signal. Move on named internal custom/total procurement dollars, counterfactual NVIDIA orders, dates of control transfer and net loss after allowance reconciliation. The challenge is a research hypothesis, not analyst guidance requiring a cut; no settled decision conflicts.

It now exceeds our base 13.57, versus 10.38 before timing revision. With revised Q3 102, tracker 376 requires Q4 133.4395 and house 385 requires 146.9395; these are our mathematical alternatives, not broker quarter estimates. Earlier one-input equivalents in analysis/2026-10-12-broker-comparison.json are archived under the old drivers [broker-oct2026].

- Before late-October reports: vendor identities, overlap methodology, nonduplicated order values and payment/control-transfer/month schedules.
- Late October 2026: customer capex actuals/guides, offset spending and site power-ready MW; named cash cuts replace/reconcile realization proxy.
- Early November 2026, expected: AMD recognized GPU-only revenue and shipment timing.
- November 18, 2026, expected/unconfirmed: NVIDIA Q3 versus 102 DC/109.5 total and Q4 guide versus own 127/required 126.58.
- January–February 2027: comparable accelerator/total-capex budgets and named custom deployment values to test the expert estimate.
- January–March 2027: receipt of deferred orders and 2027 guides; subtract rollover before calling larger orders fresh demand.

What changes the forecast: confirmed order/invoice and control-transfer schedules can deepen or reverse the partial allowance; intact October deliveries or already-recognized upstream products would make Q3/annual cuts too cautious. Named unpaid cash cuts without offsets require company-budget cuts. Quantified custom share, recognized Instinct revenue and cohort definitions move split/concentration. Revised public guidance moves capex directly. Orders are reportedly deferred, preserving ultimate demand; generic power warnings alone do not add another haircut [channel-q4-slip]. Seventeen forecast questions remain in notes/open-questions.md; no immediate repeat public search is scheduled.

## Position thesis read

No analyst guidance or settled decision conflicts with the revision. The earlier broker-driven benchmark crossing remains recorded; this is new dated timing evidence and a new information need. Analyst attention under rule 3: obtain the vendor's customer/order and acceptance-term crosswalk unavailable in the public corpus. Prior AMD/Amazon short-premise questions are not re-raised without new position-specific evidence.

NVIDIA long's calendar earnings case weakens: our base falls 3.19 and street deficit widens 1.38→4.57 (-1.22%); ultimate demand is deferred, not cancelled. AMD GPU base stays approximately at 14 street, with no claimed share gain. Whether to change positions remains the analyst's and PM's call.

Expert-watch position update: no further change to NVIDIA's 2026 long earnings case; base stays 371.43, gap -4.57 (-1.22%). AMD base stays approximately 14 street. Long-term custom capture remains a risk, not a newly quantified shortfall. No new attention trigger; the prior vendor-crosswalk question remains pending.

Analyst-challenge position update: no further movement in NVIDIA's long earnings case; base 371.43 remains4.57 below 376 (-1.22%), change against street 0. Custom displacement remains a risk, with no incremental Q4 amount established. AMDbase stays approximately 14. Position decisions remain with the analyst and PM.
